requirement:
Habeas MUST provide built-in definitions named `habeas:<name>`, available in
every project without a declaration. Each built-in MUST have fixed text, which
states its obligations and is documented in Habeas's reference documentation, and
MUST state which reference roles may use it. References MUST resolve built-in
names alongside project definitions. So that every book stands alone, the book
MUST render a reference to a built-in as a badge without a link whose hover text
gives the built-in's full text. Built-ins themselves MUST NOT require or permit
definition evidence files and MUST NOT appear as definitions in the requirements
index, `habeas status`, or the missing-evidence check of
{cite}`requirements.ci.coverage`. Per-source citation reviews under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review` MAY be required for references
to a built-in. A project definition
MUST NOT use a full name beginning with `habeas:`; validation MUST report one,
and the `:` character already makes such names invalid under
{cite}`requirements.ci.identifiers`. Validation MUST report a reference to a
built-in in a role the built-in does not permit, or that breaks the built-in's
stated form.
rationale:
I mapped each obligation of `requirements.references.builtin_definitions` to the marked tests and found no gap.

- **Built-ins exist with fixed, documented text.**
  - `src/builtins.rs#mod[tests]/fn[habeas_util_has_its_approved_text_and_permits_inline_or_fenced_citations]` checks that `habeas:util` resolves without any project declaration.
  - It checks the text's start and end, and asserts the text equals the quote in `md/reference.md`.
  - It checks that unknown names such as `habeas:other` and the removed `habeas:none` do not resolve.
  - It checks the name recogniser `is_builtin_name`.
- **Permitted roles.** The same test asserts that `check(Cite)` is OK and that `check(Impl)` and `check(Test)` fail with "built-in habeas:util may only be referenced with {cite}".
- **Names resolve alongside project definitions.** `src/fenced.rs#mod[tests]/fn[opening_fences_take_a_role_and_one_valid_or_built_in_name]` shows that `habeas:util` and the syntactically built-in `habeas:unknown` are recognised as fence names, so validation can report them. It also shows that `other:none` and invalid names stay literal. `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[cited_built_ins_contribute_their_text_and_fixmes_in_own_sites_do_not]` checks that a cited built-in contributes its text once next to a project declaration. `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[site_reviews_cite_declarations_go_stale_with_them_and_name_root_sites]` makes the same check for site reviews.
- **Book badge without a link, hover text is the full text.** `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[fenced_references_render_their_badge_and_body_and_built_ins_are_unlinked]` covers `habeas:util` and `habeas:coverage` in fenced and inline form. It asserts a `<span ... habeas-builtin title="<escaped full text>">`, no `<a ` in the inline badge, and no `href="habeas`. A project reference in the same chapter is checked to render as a link.
- **No evidence files, and no appearance in status, the index or the missing-evidence check.** `tests/references.rs#fn[built_ins_have_no_evidence_index_entry_and_are_checked_by_validation]` asserts the following:
  - A stray `evidence/habeas:util.json` is reported.
  - There is no "missing evidence for habeas:" error.
  - `habeas:` does not appear in the status table or in a status heading.
  - The book gets no detail page for a built-in.
  - The requirements index omits the built-in.
- **Citation reviews.** `tests/references.rs#fn[fenced_references_in_comments_and_built_in_rules_are_validated]` shows that only items with valid, non-`habeas:util` citations (`fn[empty]`) need a review. Items citing only `habeas:util` (`glue`), or only an unknown name (`inline`, `fenced_none`), need none. The citation-review obligation is a MAY, so nothing further is required.
- **Reserved names.** `tests/references.rs#fn[project_definitions_cannot_use_reserved_built_in_names]` asserts the reported error: names beginning with `habeas:` are reserved. It also asserts that the definition does not show up in status.
- **Invalid role or form is reported.** Wrong-role references are asserted in both a chapter and a source comment. Unknown built-ins and an unclosed fence are also asserted.

Minor observation, not a gap: `src/builtins.rs#mod[tests]/fn[coverage_builtin_uses_the_documented_text_and_only_the_citation_role]` checks the second built-in's documented text and role restriction. It carries a `{test}` reference only to `requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions.anchor`, not to this requirement. The generic mechanism is covered by the marked `habeas:util` test, and `habeas:coverage` is covered by the marked badge test in `src/lib.rs`. The requirement does not make form validation for `habeas:coverage` rationales a validation obligation. Its text criteria are assessed in citation review.

text: :::{req} builtin_definitions
Habeas MUST provide built-in definitions named `habeas:<name>`, available in
every project without a declaration. Each built-in MUST have fixed text, which
states its obligations and is documented in Habeas's reference documentation, and
MUST state which reference roles may use it. References MUST resolve built-in
names alongside project definitions. So that every book stands alone, the book
MUST render a reference to a built-in as a badge without a link whose hover text
gives the built-in's full text. Built-ins themselves MUST NOT require or permit
definition evidence files and MUST NOT appear as definitions in the requirements
index, `habeas status`, or the missing-evidence check of
{cite}`requirements.ci.coverage`. Per-source citation reviews under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review` MAY be required for references
to a built-in. A project definition
MUST NOT use a full name beginning with `habeas:`; validation MUST report one,
and the `:` character already makes such names invalid under
{cite}`requirements.ci.identifiers`. Validation MUST report a reference to a
built-in in a role the built-in does not permit, or that breaks the built-in's
stated form.
:::{req} coverage

Repository validation MUST check that every requirement defined by a fenced `{req}` directive in a chapter under the configured mdBook source directory has an evidence file named `evidence/<full-requirement-name>.json`, and MUST report each requirement whose evidence file is missing. The full name MUST use the chapter's path-derived namespace followed by the directive name; for example, a directive named `check` in `md/requirements.md` has the full name `requirements.check`.
:::{req} citation_review
Every source item outside the book that carries at least one `{cite}` reference
other than a citation of `habeas:util` under {cite}`requirements.references.util`
MUST have a citation review: an assessment of that item's citations, recorded at
`evidence/citations/<file>/<selector>.json`, where `<file>` is the item's
project-relative path, `<selector>` is its outline selector with every `/` and
`%` percent-encoded, and the root node uses `_root`. The review MUST use the
prompt defined by {cite}`requirements.authoring.citation_prompt`. For citations
of project requirements and examples, the reviewer MUST assess whether the item
should be re-checked or kept in sync when the cited definition changes, and
whether the reference procedure of
{cite}`requirements.references.procedure` calls for `{impl}` or `{test}` instead.
For citations of built-ins, the reviewer MUST check the permitted reference
roles and forms and any citation-review criteria stated in the built-in's fixed
text, using the item's source and commentary. A permitted citation role alone
MUST NOT suffice when the fixed text states additional criteria. Mandatory inputs,
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, MUST be the item's outline
node, each cited declaration or built-in text, and the citations' commentary. The record MUST contain the item's file and selector,
its citations by role, name, and commentary, `determination`, `rationale`, and
`inputs`, with determinations under {cite}`requirements.ci.outcomes`. Validation
MUST require a current, accepted review for every such item and report stale,
missing, or orphaned reviews; a review MUST become stale when the item's hash,
a cited declaration, or its citations or their commentary change. Authoring with
`--all` MUST include citation reviews, and `habeas author citations:<file>#<selector>`
MUST author the review of the one item it names, under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.refresh`, where omitting `#<selector>`
names the file's root node. A citation in a requirement or example
declaration is reviewed as part of that definition's own assessment instead.
Storage MAY use the versioned representation under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.habeas.evidence_format`, retaining the same review
information and validation rules.
:::{req} identifiers

Requirement and reference names MUST have nonempty dot-separated segments containing only ASCII letters, digits, underscores, or hyphens. A `{req}` directive whose full name is invalid, including one whose chapter path gives an invalid namespace, and a role with an invalid name MUST remain literal and MUST NOT define or reference a requirement. For nested chapter paths, a leading `reqs/` and a final `index` or `README` segment MUST be omitted from the requirement namespace.
:::{req} util
Habeas MUST provide the built-in `habeas:util` under
{cite}`requirements.references.builtin_definitions`, with this text:
> Cite this on an item that serves other code, including code outside the
> project such as a library calling a trait implementation it requires, and
> carries out no requirement or example itself: it has no obligations and no
> end-user-observable behavior of its own. A review that reaches it from a root judges what it does
> as part of that root.
Only `{cite}` MAY reference it, inline or fenced, with or without commentary. An
item whose only citations are of `habeas:util` MUST NOT need a citation review
under {cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`. This citation is optional;
helpers need no annotation merely because they serve other code.
